title: Startrails over Licancabur
caption: Star trails over Licancabur Volcano, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars trace long trails across the sky above Licancabur Volcano in this long-exposure image. Straddling the Chile–Bolivia border, the volcano is part of the Andean Central Volcanic Zone. Volcanoes of the Andes form where one of Earth's tectonic plates slides beneath another.
Licancabur is 5916 meters high, far taller than Mont Blanc, Europe's highest mountain. The photograph is credited to S. Otarola/ESO.

The trails are not caused by the stars moving. It is Earth's rotation that shifts their positions in our sky, and a long exposure records each star's apparent path as a streak of light. Stars near the celestial pole trace tight circles, while those farther away sweep out longer arcs. The longer the exposure, the longer each trail grows.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure ground-based photograph by S. Otarola. The source does not publish camera or color-processing details.
understand.eye: The eye sees stars as points. The trails appear only because the long exposure recorded Earth's rotation.
